title: Console ops-lite: single-card operational summary + focused cost/trace cuts
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description: This ticket defines a scoped, minimal feature set for the Console observability surface focused on operator use cases: a single compact 'Ops Card' for quick triage, a lightweight cost breakdown slice, and aggressive trace sampling defaults. The goal is to reduce implementation scope and run-time telemetry costs while preserving the signal needed for on-call and platform debugging. This is a deliberate MVP cut to enable a reliable launch within the release window.
background: Multiple PM and Eng prioritization sessions identified Console telemetry as a major driver of lift and recurring infra cost. Prior PRD attempted a multi-card dashboard with per-route deep dives and 100% tracing capture for problematic routes; that scope risks delaying launch and increasing hosting costs. We need a constrained MVP that surfaces essential operator signals (error rate, p50 latency, top-cost contributors) and a plan for progressive enhancement.
decisions: Ship a single, configurable Ops Card as the primary observability surface for MVP rather than multiple granular tiles
Replace full per-request tracing for all routes with 1% sampling globally and 100% sampling only for explicit canary/incident investigations
Remove per-route historical cost charts from MVP; include a single snapshot cost breakdown for the last 24h and a link to detailed billing for heavy users
Defer advanced correlation (token-level cost breakdown and trace-to-token mapping) to post-MVP roadmap
acceptance_criteria: Ops Card renders within Console route list and shows: 24h error rate, p50 latency, p95 latency, 24h cost snapshot, and top 3 tail routes by cost
Ops Card data refreshes within 60s and has backend SLA to return results within 800ms under normal load
Trace sampling defaults to 1% globally; there is a UI toggle scoped to account admins to turn on 100% sampling for a specific route for up to 24 hours
Cost snapshot uses aggregated billing data (not token-level) and calls existing cost API; per-request token cost is explicitly labeled as 'deferred' in the UI
E2E smoke tests validate the card displays for teams with >0 routes and gracefully shows 'no data' for new orgs
Console telemetry overhead (extra CPU/RPUs) for non-admin orgs must not increase overall platform observability spend by more than 10% compared to baseline measurement
notes: Trade-off: smaller surface reduces engineering time and infra cost but sacrifices fine-grained debugging for initial users
Engineering proposed an autoscaling knob for the Ops Card backend to handle dashboard storms; scope this as an implementation detail (ENG-22110)
We will include a clear CTA in the card to open a ticket / link to instructions for how to request expanded tracing during incidents
Designed to be the canonical operator landing experience for first 90 days post-launch
next_steps: Finalize API contract with ENG by 2026-03-05 (blocked until ENG-22110 API draft)
Design to deliver hi-fi Ops Card assets and responsive states by 2026-03-08
Implement backend aggregation & cost snapshot endpoint (ENG-22110) and land smoke tests
Plan a 2-week canary rollout to beta orgs with instrumentation to measure telemetry cost delta
Prepare customer communications that clearly state initial limitations and the path to richer telemetry
risks: Operators may find the single-card surface insufficient during complex incidents; mitigation: quick escalation docs and temporary sampling toggles
Underestimation of aggregation query cost causing backend spend spike; mitigation: query caps, pre-aggregations and synthetic load tests
Ambiguity in SLA wording could create support noise; mitigation: include explicit expected latencies and guide for degraded-mode behavior in release notes
